Bug_Title: BOA: Class overrides a method implemented in super class Adapter wrongly (BOA_BADLY_OVERRIDDEN_ADAPTER)
Bug_Details:
This method overrides a method found in a parent class, where that class is an Adapter that implements
a listener defined in the java.awt.event or javax.swing.event package. As a result, this method will not
get called when the event occurs.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by having the MyActionListener class extend MouseAdapter but override the actionPerformed method. Since MouseAdapter does not have an actionPerformed method, this override does nothing, and the button click event will not trigger the expected behavior.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the showBug method of the BuggyAdapter class, which simulates a button click. However, since the actionPerformed method in MyActionListener is incorrectly overridden (MyActionListener extends MouseAdapter instead of implementing ActionListener), the expected output 'Button clicked!' is never printed to the console, causing the test to fail.
